x: Mayiladumparai (Krishnagiri district, Tamil Nadu) is AMS-dated to 2172 BCE and is described as the earliest iron-use evidence in India. Sivagalai (Thoothukudi) is the site with iron dated to about 2953 BCE, Thirumalapuram (Tenkasi) has an Iron Age urn chamber, and Adichanallur is the type-site for urn burials.

Govikartana was the king's companion in the chase and keeper of game, not the chief priest; the chief priest was the Purohita. Gramani (village headman), Mahishi (chief queen) and Kshata/Kshatri (chamberlain) are correctly matched.
Madhyadesha was the middle region. Aryavarta was the north (not south), Dakshinapatha the south (not north), and Videha lay in north Bihar to the east, beyond the Sadanira (Gandak), not in the west.

Painted Grey Ware is grey pottery with linear painted designs, mostly bowls and dishes, of the Later Vedic period (c. 1000-600 BCE). Highly polished black pottery describes NBPW (from c. 600 BCE), ochre-coloured pottery is OCP, and red pottery with black interiors describes Black and Red Ware.
